newsitem.title: UK: Coffee prices up seven percent on Brazil crop news.
newsitem.headline: Coffee prices up seven percent on Brazil crop news.

text.p: Coffee prices surged by seven percent in brisk London trading on Tuesday, buoyed by forecasts of a lower Brazilian crop.
"The Brazilian news triggered investment fund buying on fears of a shortage of coffee supplies," said a trader.

The head of the primary commodities department of Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry forecast on Monday that the country's 1997/98 crop would reach only 18-20 million 60-kg bags versus 25 million in 1996/97.
Brazil is the biggest coffee grower and exporter.
Robusta coffee on the London futures market jumped seven percent to $1,473 a tonne basis March in early trading, the highest since September last year.
By 1530 GMT, the contract traded at $1,437, still $57 up on the day. Coffee was below $1,300 at the end of 1996.

It has been on a steady advance since then and is now also being supported by a possibility that producer nations, who meet in Brazil on Thursday, may try to tighten export curbs to lock in firmer prices.
African producers, led by Ivory Coast, want the 14-member Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) to trim exports in the first half of 1997 by 2.5 million bags.
Returning from Vietnam, Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze told Reuters on Monday that Hanoi - not an ACPC member - had expressed support for the ACPC and would consider joining.
But Vietnamese industry officials said on Tuesday that it considered joining the ACPC but lacked the administrative or financial capability to participate in export curbs just now.
Vietnam is Asia's second largest coffee producer after Indonesia. ACPC-member Indonesia was said to have softened its opposition to the African plan for new export curbs.
But industry sources said Jakarta's agreement to participate in the scheme would hinge on how much it would have to reduce exports.
"If we restrain our supplies, there are free riders in the region who will take our market," a senior Indonesian official has said. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
